Set piece: east of Eden. The man and the woman, clothed in skins, walking east out of the garden at dusk, seen from behind, the trees ending, a wide dry land opening before them. Behind them, in the eastern opening between the great trees, fire: a whirling sword of flame, a long blade of living fire turning in the air, its light flashing on the trunks; around it, vast shapes of wings made of flame and shadow, never faces, never figures. The camera pulls back and up until they are two specks in the dark land and the flame is a single point of fire behind them.

In the eastern opening of the garden at dusk, cherubim standing guard, towering between the great trees, their wings of fire spread, firelight on the trunks. The cherubim are as the prophet Ezekiel describes them: towering beings, each with four faces, the face of a man at the front, the face of a lion on the right, the face of an ox on the left and the face of an eagle behind; four great wings, two spread wide with their tips touching, two folded down covering the body; human hands beneath the wings; straight legs with feet like a calf's hoof gleaming like burnished bronze; fire moving back and forth among them with flashes of light; their wings edged with living flame. Never winged children, never robed people with wings, no rings of light over their heads. No human figures.
